examples.problem: The mean height of a group of basketball players is $178\textrm{ cm}$. A player in this group is $184\textrm{ cm}$ tall and his $z$-score is $z = 1.5$. Find the standard deviation of the basketball players' heights.
examples.worked_solution:
To compute the value of an observation $x$ which yields a given $z$-score in a data set with mean $\overline{x}$ and standard deviation $\sigma,$ we can use the following formula:

$$
x = \overline{x} + z \cdot \sigma
$$

Substituting $x=184,$ $\overline{x}=178,$ and $z=1.5$ into the formula and solving for $\sigma,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\overset{―}{x}+z\cdot \sigma  \\ 184 & =178+1.5\cdot \sigma  \\ 6 & =1.5\cdot \sigma  \\ \sigma  & =\frac{6}{1.5} \\ \sigma  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the standard deviation of the players heights is $4\,\textrm{cm}.$
